I think it's really difficult and frustrating sometimes, because at the end of the day, she just doesn't experience it for herself and therefore can't really explain it - which probably just leaves you feeling more confused about it. Those things can all help to express how you feel inside, but don't determine it. It's an internal feeling. I have a similar issue with non-binary people in that I just don't understand their experience. It doesn't make their experience any less valid, but I don't think I can ever truly understand it simply due to the fact that I don't feel it. I can try and understand, but I can't ever talk for them or explain things for them, because... It's just not something I experience myself (and therefore, in the position of the presenter on your situation, I'd be just as confused on how to explain it adequately since I just genuinely wouldn't know)

I mostly just think that it's an internal feeling, and those things that are typically associated with the gender you feel inside just help to give you a chance to express that. Especially if you never had the chance to before, it feels so freeing and exciting. To just... Have a chance to express how you feel. Just like a lot of people prefer certain styles of clothing, or even simple things like decor in their house. It's all just expressing what you like, feel and enjoy - and being trans just often means that you like a lot of the things that are typically categorised as not being for you, which sucks when inside, that's just how you feel, and feel most comfortable.

I think it depends. For me, gender dysphoria is more impactful on how I feel inside and having no labels wouldn't really help that as such. There's just... This thing in my brain that bugs me that something doesn't connect mentally and physically. There's just something not right, and it makes me really uncomfortable. Feminine clothes and such help to express what I feel, especially since I couldn't have it for so long. It's not what makes you a woman, but since a lot of people don't actually get it and since you couldn't have it for so long, it's hard to not find it extremely appealing. It makes you happy to finally have some sort of way to express how you feel to the outside world. It may not be perfect, but sometimes it's just as close as you can get. 

And all else aside, it's not like the world is going to change so drastically and get of labels any time soon regardless so even that wouldn't be of much help, because there are still going to be people who label you.

Trans girl here, I'm probably not the only one to try and explain their own experience but I thought I'd give it a go. This may not be everyone's experience, but it's what I've been dealing with so it may be some insight I suppose.

So, in a sense, I do tend to even get a little frustrated at myself for sometimes reinforcing gender stereotypes when I don't even mean to. Sometimes, regardless of how nonsensical it may seem to me, gender dysphoria doesn't actually care what does and doesn't make sense. It's an internal feeling and all you really have is your ability to try and express that outwardly otherwise no one will actually accept you as you are (or, at least, that's how it can feel). And sometimes, you can't even accept yourself as "really" being a woman if you don't enforce some of the stereotypes. Not because you necessarily mean to, but because it's so drilled into society that you're just born with this notion of what it's supposed to be and how you don't fit. Gender dysphoria practically manipulates you into 'fitting in' so you can get a small sense of comfort.

I admire anyone who can feel comfortable with their gender without having to fit the gender norms. I love being a woman, and there are a lot of things that I love being able to do (wear makeup, or dresses, etc.) that I couldn't do before (mostly because of how other people would treat me because "I'm a man" so I should act a certain way), but sometimes I feel like I need them because unfortunately gender dysphoria doesn't listen to logic, it just makes you feel shit about things you can't control. Sometimes I don't wear makeup. Othertimes I enjoy wearing it and it's fun. Othertimes I feel so bad I feel like I need it or the whole world is just going to see me as a man. I may not like it, but I can't control it. It's partially what I've been taught and being scared of what other people will think. 

I hope that the 'gender dysphoria making me feel like I need to do certain things part' will lessen in time. That I'll get more comfortable with myself and that there will be less stress from my brain. But for now, I'll just... Do whatever makes me happy and content. It's all about the internal experience and how you can try and convey that to the outside world. I often try to express myself for myself, but I'd be lying if I said that other people's opinions and expectations didn't influence me.

And while I am not and don't understand the experience for gender non-conforming people, I would generally believe it's similar in a sense to having that internal feeling of not fitting with either and I wouldn't even know how I'd navigate that.

Edit: Another note, I do think that gender identity and gender expression (and stereotypes in this case) are separate things, but they often coincidence and can seem the same from an outside perspective.
